subject: Reserved capacity proposal and pricing sensitivity — ZenithBio pilot
messages:
From: Sarah Lin <sarah@zenithbio.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 5 Nov 2025 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Capacity planning & pricing sensitivity for upcoming pilot

Hi Logan,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with Redwood's latency numbers. We're trying to firm up the infrastructure budget for our Q1 pilot and need clarity on reserved capacity terms. A couple of asks from procurement and engineering: 

- Can you share a committed-capacity pricing proposal for a 6–12 month reserved tenor, plus a lighter 3-month pilot option?
- How sensitive are discounts/pricing to GPU market movement? Procurement is pushing for a clause that protects us if GPU spot / list prices spike.
- We expect peak concurrent inference of ~1200 tokens/sec (80 GPUs equivalent) during inference-heavy experiments, with a lower baseline (~20% of peak) for the first two months.

Attached is a rough SRE traffic profile and our internal forecast. Can you loop in pricing and ops so we can get a mutual action plan?

Thanks,
Sarah
Sarah Lin
Head of Platform Engineering, ZenithBio
[Attachment: zenith_sre_traffic_profile.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah@zenithbio.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 6 Nov 2025 10:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity planning & pricing sensitivity for upcoming pilot

Sarah — thanks for the clear ask and the traffic profile. Appreciated.

High level response up front: we can support both a short 3-month pilot and a 6–12 month reserved commit. To be conservative for budgeting we recommend an initial 3-month pilot with a convertible reserved commitment at month 3 (so you get the lower committed pricing once you convert).

I've attached a short proposal and a GPU-cost sensitivity workbook that lays out three scenarios (base, +20% GPU cost, +40% GPU cost) and how pricing/discounts flow through to unit token cost. Highlights: 

- 3-month pilot (non-committed): on-demand rates, with a small pilot credit we can offer (one-time).
- 6-month reserved (50 GPU equivalent baseline, burst to 80): 18% discount off list in base case.
- 12-month reserved (same baseline): 24% discount in base case.
- Conditional GPU indexation: if GPU market cost > 25% above the base index we propose a pass-through adjustment partially shared (we absorb up to 10% of the delta; remainder applied as a modest surcharge or credit mechanism depending on which side is triggered).

Operational asks: finalizing the proposal needs a breakdown of peak vs sustained usage (your SRE sheet helps) and a target start date.

Next steps I'm proposing:
1) You review attached "zenith_capacity_proposal_v2.pdf" and the "gpu_cost_sensitivity.xlsx".
2) Karthik and David to confirm approval path for discounts >20% and whether the conditional indexation model is acceptable.
3) If OK, we'll issue a DocuSign for signature and route for procurement.

Attachments: zenith_capacity_proposal_v2.pdf (proposal, 3 pages); gpu_cost_sensitivity.xlsx (workbook, 4 sheets)

Best,
Logan Wright
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
[Cell: +1 415 555 0192]

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 7 Nov 2025 15:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Capacity planning & pricing sensitivity for upcoming pilot

Logan / David — reviewed the workbook. A few notes for the approval path and internal risk: 

1) Discount thresholds: our standard approval matrix allows up to 18% discount at quota-level sign-off. Anything 18%–28% needs Director approval; >28% requires CRO sign-off + rev commit > $350k ARR. The 24% 12-month line you proposed falls in Director territory — we can route, but please flag to the customer that exec sign-off may add 5–7 business days.

2) GPU indexation mechanism: the conditional pass-through model is okay but we need contract language that caps total pass-through to protect Redwood. Recommend: a cap at 30% of base GPU cost with a tiered split (Redwood covers first 10% of spike, customer covers next 20%). Karthik to own creating the clause text.

3) SKU allocation / burst pools: ops (David) — confirm whether we can guarantee a burst pool up to +60% of baseline for a pilot-to-prod ramp without disrupting other reserved pools. If not, propose an explicit burst SLA window.

4) Revenue accounting / deal_id: please ensure HubSpot deal ZEN-2025-144 has the projected commit and expected start date so finance can pre-approve crediting. HubSpot: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/51234-ZEN-2025-144

I can start the approval thread once Logan confirms the final committed numbers (baseline GPUs, tenor, and proposed discount).

- Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Director, Strategic Pricing, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: internal_approval_checklist.pdf (1 page)]

From: Logan Wright <logan_wright@redwood.ai>
To: Sarah Lin <sarah@zenithbio.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, David Kim <david_kim@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 19 Nov 2025 11:40:00 -0800
Subject: Reserved capacity proposal and next steps (ZenithBio)

Sarah — looping back with a finalized recommendation after internal review. Quoting your ask below for context.

> "Can you share a committed-capacity pricing proposal for a 6–12 month reserved tenor, plus a lighter 3-month pilot option? How sensitive are discounts/pricing to GPU market movement?"

Final proposal summary (attached PDF):
- Pilot: 3 months non-committed, pilot credit = $25k one-time; on-demand rates otherwise.
- Committed option A (6 months): baseline 50 GPU eq., burst to 80 for scheduled windows; discount = 18% in base index case.
- Committed option B (12 months): baseline 50 GPU eq., discount = 24% in base index case.
- Conditional GPU indexation: as discussed, cap at 30% of base GPU cost, Redwood absorbs first 10% of index spike; remainder split per the draft clause (see attached).

Approval note: Option B at 24% will require Director approval on our side (Karthik flagged this) and may add ~1 week for internal sign-off. Anything above 28% would need CRO approval and higher revenue thresholds.

Action items / next steps:
- If you accept option B, confirm baseline start date and I will route for internal Director approval.
- If you prefer to start with pilot -> convert, confirm pilot start window and we will prepare a convertible amendment that preserves the offered discounts upon conversion.
- DocuSign ready: https://www.docusign.com/zenith/ZN-2025-144

Attachments: zenith_capacity_proposal_v2.pdf; gpu_cost_sensitivity.xlsx

Thanks — happy to jump on a quick call if procurement wants to walk through the indexation language.

Best,
Logan Wright
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
